verdict: BEAM 100K tier measured end-to-end through the local-reproducible adapter (design path A); hybrid tracks rag overall while cortex-only lags badly outside abstention — the per-ability breakdown, not the headline, is the finding

run.extractor: qwen-27b (dream pass, v5 op prompt, drain-until-empty per batch)
run.answer_judge: qwen3.6-27b on the reproducible q8_0 server (evals/qwen_server.ps1 Start-Qwen; never -Fast for judged output)
run.note: run spanned two sessions (rows 1-240 on 2026-08-02, rows 241-400 overnight 2026-08-03 after a user GPU pause; resumable-by-row worked as designed). Rows 241-400 ran on a user-applied GPU curve (950mV / 2670MHz / +1000 mem); in-run canaries clean (0 judge failures, throughput on trend, coherent output).

results_intfaithful.note: upstream BEAM code int()-floors per-rubric-item scores (0.5 -> 0); both scorings recorded per row, divergence documented rather than silently fixed

abstention.note: small curated fact context abstains correctly where raw-turn context invites confabulation

weakest_hybrid.note: all three need cross-batch aggregation or ordering that per-fact consolidation discards

cross_bench_convergence: The companion LongMemEval all-types run (longmemeval-all-oracle-qwen-27b-alltypes-0803) shows the same shape: hybrid excels on canonical-fact types (knowledge-update 0.910, single-session-user 0.957, single-session-assistant 0.964) and falls below the raw-turns rag control exactly where aggregation across sessions or time is required (multi-session 0.383 vs rag 0.504; temporal-reasoning 0.534 vs 0.526; single-session-preference 0.600 vs 0.800). Two independent benchmarks agree: the system's gap is cross-session aggregation/ordering, not fact fidelity.
caveats: NOT comparable to published BEAM numbers (Mem0, Hindsight, etc.): those use a GPT-4o judge; this run judges with local qwen3.6-27b for reproducibility. Cross-system comparison requires re-judging with the paper's judge, a deliberate open decision.
Single replicate; no significance claims. The rag arm is the identical-input control across future reruns.
qwen-27b extractor arm only; the production dreamer (claude-opus-5 via shim) arm is future work and would cost API tokens.
decision: Adapter and artifacts committed; BEAM joins the harness set. Next leverage item per both benches: aggregation-aware recall (event ordering / multi-session synthesis), not further extractor fidelity work.
